confirm.text: This is a gas reading above zero and a stop-work that was actually exercised. Note that the form's multi-select records only "Stop work authority was discussed" — not "utilized" — and the Learn section is entirely blank, so the event exists only in free text. Follow-up: confirm the reading and the source with Galindo, and have the stop-work recorded properly.
6. Jordan Lemmons — XTO, CHEATHAM 13 #5, job 35896, ended 11:56 AM. Benzene was detected during a well blowdown.
"Blew down the well and tested got some benzene so let it air out and got 0s"

The close-out adds: "Blew down well from 800 psi and got it down to 200 and the well clogged up so stopped and disconnected everything we were getting straight oil from the well". The atmosphere cleared to zero, but the detection, the clog and the stoppage are not reflected anywhere in the structured fields — the multi-select carries one item, "Job scope completed safely and as planned". Follow-up: confirm the reading and whether respiratory protection was in use.
7. 1099 Baldemar Bracamontes — XTO, SPRABERRY DRIVER 2272A, job 36063, OWL submitted 9:55 AM. An energized line was found connected to the wellhead during the pre-job walk.

"Roustabout crew and safety crew walked the location together to see what potential triggers were present, found a cathodic line that was still live and connected to the wellhead, MT went to shut it off before work started."

The hazard was identified and corrected before work began, which is the system working. It is flagged because "Unsafe conditions" was not selected on the form, so this would not surface in any count. Follow-up: none required on the job itself; worth using as a positive example.
8. 1099 Baldemar Bracamontes — XTO, SPRABERRY DRIVER 2271A, job 36071, ended 4:17 PM. The Learn section describes personnel under a suspended load.
"Be more careful with the crane guys, not let them stand under suspended load"

This sits against an Observe narrative on the same form stating "Job was completed without incident". Follow-up: confirm with Bracamontes whether personnel were in fact under a suspended load and whether it was corrected at the time; if so, this is a life-saving-rule item for the crane crew.
9. Michael Hutt — XTO / FESCO, Lilly #1, Taylor, AR — H2S daily, form time 6:58 PM, board AT# 609. One cascade bottle is recorded far below the others.
"Pressure on Cascade System: 1@900/1@4300/2@4400"
No threshold is set on the form, so this is raised for confirmation rather than called a failure. Follow-up: confirm whether the 900 psi bottle is in service and needs changing out.
10. 1099 Benjamin Boutte — SM Energy, Junior Mint Fed Com 223H — H2S daily, form time 4:59 PM. Equipment reported left behind, in "Comments or Concerns for Management".
"1 Otis senior left behind in trailer 502. It came off that flow back side"
No notified party is named, and the trailer he names (502) is not the trailer the board assigns to his job (503). Follow-up: locate the sensor and confirm which trailer it is in.
Stop work / unsafe conditions — needs confirmation, not action

These are selections on the air job multi-select, not confirmed events. Per Kelby Hammer's 09/23 guidance, technicians may be selecting "Unsafe conditions" because they regard wellhead work as inherently unsafe rather than because a specific condition arose. No form filed on 10/21 selected "Stop work authority utilized." Every stop-work selection on the day was the routine pre-job item, "Stop work authority was discussed."
"Unsafe conditions" selected with no narrative anywhere on the form describing an unsafe condition — four forms, two technicians:
1099 William "Jimmy" Cooper — XTO, LOCKLAR HOLIMAN 28C 103H, job 36069. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". The only narrative is "Great team work between 2 crews".
1099 William "Jimmy" Cooper — XTO, LOCKLAR HOLIMAN 28B 102H, job 36057. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". The only narrative is "Teamwork".

Ralph Forbes — XTO, LOCKLAR HOLIMAN 28B 102H, job 36056. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". The narrative says "Set up exclusion zone conducted a conversion on two Wells. All work completed no issues." — which contradicts the selection.

1099 Gage Gonzales — XTO, MCMASTER A 1402, job 36059. Also selected "Stop work authority was discussed". The narrative names activity types only — "WAME, Breaking containment, critical lifting" — and the Win narrative says "Job carried out without unplanned stops".

Forms selecting "Stop work authority was discussed" with no unsafe-conditions item and nothing in the narrative — routine, listed for completeness: Bryan Medlin (35998), Ralph Forbes (36068), 1099 Bobby Galindo (35587), Jeremy Norris (36054), Michael Jobe (36092_1 and 36098_1), Alexander Clubb (36097_1), Dawson Drake (35978), 1099 Kedrick McCarter (36037 and 35897).

Four forms are not the mis-selection pattern and should be treated separately. In three of them a real condition is described in the narrative while the selection understates it, and in one a stoppage is described with no detail at all: Bobby Galindo's LEL of 17 on job 36055 (stop-work actually exercised, only "discussed" selected); Jordan Lemmons' benzene detection on job 35896 (a single generic item selected); Baldemar Bracamontes' live cathodic line on job 36063 ("Unsafe conditions" not selected at all); and 1099 Kedrick McCarter on CHEATHAM 13 #5, job 35897, whose narrative reads "We blew down the well from 800 to 200 psi had to stop bleeding the after some minor issues MT stopped the job" — a customer-initiated stoppage with the issues unnamed, no corrective action recorded, and Suspended Time left blank. All four are covered above or warrant a direct conversation with the technicia

On repeats: Michael Jobe appeared on this list twice on 09/26 with "Unsafe conditions" and no supporting narrative; he did not select it on either of his forms today. Nathan Contreras, also on the 09/26 list, filed no job forms today. Jimmy Cooper and Gage Gonzales are new to this list.

One further pattern: the same nine-item multi-select string appears verbatim on ten separate forms today across eight technicians. That is consistent with a selection being carried forward rather than made fresh, which is the training point Kelby raised.

clean.text: Nothing required attention on the following. Nathan Contreras filed two clean Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 152. Luis Zarate filed two clean Trailer Inspection Forms for trailer 608 and the XBC Giddings air job (36090_2), which carried the most complete OWL close-out of the day. Bryan Medlin filed three Trailer Inspection Forms and the Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 603, all complete. Jerry Gonzales filed two Trailer Inspection Forms and the Trailer Readiness Form for trailer 606, all complete. Jordan Lemmons' trailer paperwork for 601 — two inspections and the readiness form — was complete and clean. Larry Taylor's H2S daily (Comstock, Patterson 904) and Rolando Flores' H2S daily (Ovintiv, Terlingua) were both clean once the lights-and-sirens exemption and the AT# "N/A" exemption are applied. Shelby Gibbs' EOG fit test and Keelan Hammer's EOG DPO class were complete.

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based. A defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside the images, not as text, so this review can confirm that a photo was attached and when it was captured, but not what it shows. One further limitation specific to this run: it executed at 11:00 PM Central, minutes after the day closed, so the usual sweep of the following morning for late-arriving submissions could not be performed. Any 10/21 form that lands on the morning of 10/22 is not included here.

85 of 85 submissions read. Both job boards were available — the 10/21/2026 ArkLaTex and Permian Basin boards sent by Blake Walton at 10:07 AM — and the 10-21 sheet of each was used. 48 manned rows were checked on the Permian board and 11 on the ArkLaTex board, 59 in total, after excluding rows marked CANCELLED, ON STANDBY, DAYS OFF, WTX SUPPORT and shop.
